trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day trip: roughly 6 hours up the couloir to a bivy at the C-J col, then a brutal 18-20+ hour summit day on the East Ridge and back down to the trailhead.

days.title: Approach to the C-J col bivy
days.objective: Climb the couloir to the bivy at the C-J col
days.note: Walk a short way back down the road from the Cascade Pass trailhead, drop through brush into the valley and cross the Cascade River, then cross the moraine to the apron of the couloir at about 3,300 ft, roughly twenty minutes from the road. days.title: Couloir, East Ridge, summit, and full reversal
days.objective: Climb the CJ Couloir and East Ridge to the summit, then reverse the entire route to the trailhead
days.note: An alpine start from the col bivy onto the East Ridge, then sustained, loose, exposed 3rd-5th class climbing along the ridge to the true summit. camps_on_file.name: Cascade-Johannesburg Col bivy
camps_on_file.notes: Top of the CJ Couloir between Cascade Peak and Johannesburg. Most parties sleep here and climb to the summit the next morning.

camps_on_file.name: Johannesburg Camp
camps_on_file.notes: A walk-in camp a short, steep and often slick few minutes above the Cascade Pass trailhead at the end of the road — not a drive-up campground, you carry everything in. trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day, one-bivy trip for most parties: ~10 hours climbing the lower buttress to a 7,100 ft bivy, then a very long second day finishing the route (only ~2-2.5 hours to the summit from the high bivy) and descending Doug's Direct back to the trailhead, often after dark.

days.title: Climb the lower buttress to high bivy
days.objective: Climb the lower buttress to the 7,100 ft bivy at the base of the summit glacier
days.note: From the Cascade Pass trailhead, cross the valley and climb steep brush, tree-climbing, loose slabs, and heather onto the buttress proper, then pitch out lower rock to reach a bivy at the base of the upper glacier/snow arete. This is the crux logistical day — 8-12 hours is typical.

days.title: Finish the buttress, summit, and descend Doug's Direct
days.objective: Finish the remaining pitches to the summit, then descend Doug's Direct to the trailhead
days.note: A short but technical push from the high bivy — snow arete, glacier crossing, and a final ice pitch — reaches the summit in about 2-2.5 hours. The descent is the long part: downclimbing/rappelling (up to ~7-8 raps) to the C-J col, then traversing beneath Cascade Peak and the Triplets and over Mixup Peak's north ridge b…

camps_on_file.name: Buttress bivy at the heather-to-rock transition
camps_on_file.notes: This is a planned bivy, not an emergency ledge, and it is what makes the route a two-day climb for most parties — it typically takes eight to twelve hours of climbing from the base of the buttress to reach it, with two to three hours of glacier and summit snow above. It sits where the steep heather and rock give way to…

camps_on_file.name: Chopped platforms on the upper glacier
camps_on_file.notes: An improvised, secondary option above the standard bivy for parties who ran out of daylight higher up. Summer sun cupping means real work with an axe to get a flat platform, and it is fully exposed to wind and to crevasse hazard, so probe and anchor. Treat this as an emergency bivy rather than a plan.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day push: climb the forested and heathery rib from the car to a 7,100 ft bivy below the snow arete, then summit early and descend the East Ridge and Doug's Direct back to Cascade Pass trailhead.

days.title: Car to bivy ledge on the rib
days.objective: Climb the rib to the bivy ledge below the glacier
days.note: From the Cascade Pass trailhead, cross the Cascade River and the moraine, then get onto the rock via the avalanche moat (~4,400 ft). Expect brushy 4th-class tree climbing, heather and some low-5th rock. Abegg's party took about 8 hours to cover roughly 1 mile and 3,500 ft to the bivy at 7,100 ft.

days.title: Summit, East Ridge and Doug's Direct out
days.objective: Summit, then descend the East Ridge and hike out over Mixup
days.note: It is about an hour from the bivy up the snow arete to the summit. Traverse the gendarmes on loose 3rd/4th-class ledges about 75 ft below the crest, then rappel (about 7 raps) or downclimb to the Cascade-Johannesburg col, roughly 3 hours. Don't drop straight off the col because of ice and rockfall. Take Doug's Direct o…

days.title: Day 2

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip covering ~12 miles round trip and ~2,900 ft of net gain to the basin camp, with a short but slow (loose, exposed class 3-4) summit day on Katsuk from camp; most parties tag neighboring Mesahchie Peak the same day via the connecting gullies.

days.note: Hike the well-graded Easy Pass Trail to the 6,550 ft pass, then leave the trail and sidehill traverse west across scree, talus, and grassy benches at roughly 6,600-6,800 ft to the basin camp south of Mesahchie Peak. days.title: Summit day: Katsuk (and often Mesahchie)
days.objective: Climb Katsuk Peak via the Southwest Gully
days.note: From camp, climb loose talus to the small col/pass below Katsuk, then work up the complex system of gullies, ramps, and slabs of the Southwest Gully to just below the mushroom-shaped summit block. The final class 4 summit block is short but exposed and is usually the crux both ways. Many parties link Katsuk with neighb…

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Easy Pass trailhead
days.note: Reverse the Day 1 traverse and descent: sidehill back to Easy Pass, then descend the maintained trail to the trailhead.

campsite_pins.name: Basin camp south of Mesahchie Peak

trip_plan.totalNote: Hike 4.9 miles over Cascade Pass to Pelton Basin Camp, then climb the Yawning Glacier and the 600 ft north face to the summit and hike out on day two.

days.title: Hike over Cascade Pass to Pelton Basin
days.objective: Set up camp at Pelton Basin and scout the route
days.note: Hike 4.9 miles to Pelton Basin Camp (1,800 ft of gain) and set up camp. Scout the couloir and glacier entry from the basin in evening light.

days.title: Climb the North Face and hike out
days.objective: Summit via the Yawning Glacier and north face
days.note: Make a pre-dawn start and climb the couloir and Yawning Glacier to the Magic–Pelton Col, cross the head of the glacier, and climb the 600 ft north face to the notch and the summit. Either reverse the glacier or descend the South Ridge and loop back over Cache Col to Cascade Pass, then hike out.

camps_on_file.name: Pelton Basin

trip_plan.totalNote: Hike 4.9 miles over Cascade Pass to Pelton Basin Camp, then climb the Yawning Glacier and the northeast couloir to the summit and hike out on day two.

days.title: Hike over Cascade Pass to Pelton Basin

days.note: Hike 4.9 miles over Cascade Pass to Pelton Basin Camp and set up. Look at the couloir in evening light to pick your line and identify the overhead hazard.

days.title: Climb the couloir and hike out
days.objective: Summit via the Yawning Glacier and couloir
days.note: Make a very early start up the couloir approach and the Yawning Glacier to the Magic–Pelton Col, then climb the couloir to the summit. Descend either the couloir, early while it is frozen, or the South Ridge, then hike out.

trip_plan.totalNote: Hike over Cascade Pass and Cache Col to camp at Kool-Aid Lake, then climb the northwest ridge, descend the South Ridge, and exit over Cache Col on day two.

days.title: Hike over Cache Col to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Camp at Kool-Aid Lake
days.note: Hike 3.7 miles to Cascade Pass, continue over the Cache Glacier and Cache Col, and drop to Kool-Aid Lake to camp (5.9 miles, about 5 hours).

days.title: Climb the Northwest Ridge and hike out
days.objective: Summit, return to camp, and exit over Cache Col
days.note: Cross to the base of the northwest ridge and climb it and the northwest face to the summit. Descend the South Ridge back to camp, then pack up and hike out over Cache Col.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-night, 3-day trip is the norm: hike in to Kool-Aid Lake camp, a long summit day on the South Ridge from camp, then hike out — 5,000+ ft of gain/loss total. A few very fit, fast parties push it car-to-car in one very long (14-18 hr) day, but off-trail travel, route-finding on the ridge, and the wilderness permit make an overnight the standard approach.

days.title: Approach to Kool-Aid Lake camp
days.objective: Establish camp at Kool-Aid Lake via Cascade Pass and Cache Col
days.note: From the Cascade Pass trailhead, switchback up the maintained trail to Cascade Pass, then leave trail and climb cross-country north to Cache Col. Descend snow/heather on the far side to Kool-Aid Lake (~6,120 ft), the standard camp for Magic Mountain and the Ptarmigan Traverse's southern end.

days.objective: Climb Magic Mountain via the South Ridge and return to camp
days.note: An alpine-start day from camp: climb roughly 1,000 ft to the 7,100 ft col between Magic Mountain and Hurry Up Peak, then follow heather and rock (class 3) up the South Ridge to the false summit. days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Break camp and return to the trailhead
days.note: Pack up and reverse the approach: back over Cache Col and down to Cascade Pass, then out the maintained trail to the car. Many parties combine this with a side trip up nearby Hurry Up Peak or a scenic detour if time and weather allow.

trip_plan.totalNote: Hike over Cascade Pass and Cache Col to camp at Kool-Aid Lake, then climb the southwest cirque, descend the South Ridge, and exit over Cache Col on day two.

days.title: Climb the Southwest Cirque and hike out
days.objective: Summit, return to camp, and exit over Cache Col
days.note: Climb into the southwest cirque and take a gully to the summit ridge and the top (2-3 hours). Descend the South Ridge to camp, then pack up and exit over Cache Col.

camps_on_file.name: Johannesburg Camp
camps_on_file.notes: A walk-in camp a short, steep and often slick few minutes above the Cascade Pass trailhead at the end of the road — not a drive-up campground, you carry everything in. It is the practical staging point for the Cascade-Johannesburg Couloir, Cascade Peak, and any pre-dawn start where you want to be at the road end the ni…

trip_plan.totalNote: A remote multi-day trip: two or three days of mostly off-trail travel each way over Kindy Ridge and the Buckindy high country, with one roped glacier-and-Class-4 summit day from a camp below the north side.

days.title: Approach over Kindy Ridge toward the head of Kindy Creek
days.objective: Reach a camp at the head of Kindy Creek below Buckindy's north side (two or three days from the car)
days.note: From the FR-1570 pullout walk the brushy, washed-out roadbed almost 2 miles to its end, then climb the steep climbers' trail more than two miles through old growth onto Kindy Ridge and the saddle south of Point 5116, near 4,800 ft. From there the way to Buckindy goes south off trail through the Buckindy Range high coun…

days.title: Summit day via the Kindy/Goat Creek Glacier
days.objective: Climb Buckindy's north side glacier and Class 4 summit block
days.note: An early roped start across the glacier to dodge crevasses in firm morning snow, then a push to the base of the summit block for Class 4 scrambling to the top. The return reverses the same line, staying roped through the crevassed sections back to camp.

days.title: Hike out over Kindy Ridge
days.objective: Return over Kindy Ridge to the car
days.note: Break camp and reverse the approach: back north through the high country to the Kindy Ridge saddle, then down the steep climbers' trail and the brushy roadbed to the FR-1570 pullout. Like the way in, this usually takes more than one day.

camps_on_file.name: Head of Kindy Creek and the Kindy-Buck Creek pass
camps_on_file.notes: The ground that puts Mount Buckindy in range. Buckindy's standard route is a class 4 scramble on the north slopes, with glaciers on the north and east flanks, and the parties who climb it are camping either in the basins at the head of Kindy Creek or at the pass between the Kindy and Buck Creek drainages. Coming in fro…

camps_on_file.name: Horse Lake saddle camp
camps_on_file.notes: First-night camp on the Green Mountain approach, past the south shoulder of Green Mountain. Beyond it the traverse toward Misch and Buckindy is slow sidehill travel.

trip_plan.totalNote: A standard 2-day trip: ~10 miles and 4,600 ft round trip, but the pathless, brushy approach is the real crux, which is why most parties camp at ~6,100 ft rather than push it car-to-car. Very strong, route-savvy parties have compressed it into a single long day (14-16+ hrs) via the shorter western approach, but that is the exception, not the norm.

days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach camp on the heather bench below the west face (~6,100 ft)
days.note: Drive Highway 530 to Illabot Creek Road (FR-16) and park near the Arrow Creek switchback (~2,220 ft). The approach is notoriously pathless and arduous — old logging road, then a rough fisherman's trail through brush and forest, then steep sidehilling through gullies and heather to a bench camp below the west face/west …

days.title: Summit push and hike out
days.objective: Climb the west-face/west-ridge ramp to the 7,127 ft summit, then descend all the way to the car
days.note: From camp, ascend heather benches to the west ridge ramp and follow easy but exposed Class 2-3 terrain (some solid low-angle rock and loose sections) to the summit. Reverse the route back through camp, break camp, and continue the long descent out to the trailhead the same day.

camps_on_file.name: Jug Lake
camps_on_file.notes: The base for Mount Chaval, which sits immediately southwest of Snowking and has three standard approaches and one longer non-standard one, none of them simple and all of them brushy.
